text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- French president Jacques Chirac congratulates President Franjo Tudjman on his re-election as Croatian head of state.
- Croatian customs services arrive on the five Croat-Yugoslav border crossings in Eastern Slavonia.

- Fans planning to attend the Partizan (Belgrade) and Croatia (Zagreb) UEFA cup football match next Wednesday in Belgrade will go through rigorous double-checks of both police and local stadium staff for reasons of safety.
- UN Security Council extends the UNTAES mandate until January 15, 1998 and decides on a substantial scaling-down of troops.
- The Croatian educaton system to be introduced in Eastern Slavonia on September 1.
- Health Minister Andrija Hebrang visits the Vukovar hospital.
- Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) to ensure 56 million kuna worth of loans for nine companies in the Sibenik region.
- Representatives from 18 Croatian counties, apart from the Zadar and Brodska Posavina counties have been elected to the Serb National Council (SNV) Assembly.
- An explosion destroys an OSCE vehicle in Zvornik.
- McDonald's is planning to open a total of 30 restaurants across Croatia.
VECERNJI LIST
- The British documentary "True Stories - The Grave" on the Ovcara mass grave has its Zagreb premiere.
- The intitial reactions of foreign visitors leaving the Croatian coasts are favourable with special praise being given to Porec and Makarska.
- Viktor Lenac ship repair company is listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.
- Croatian ambassador to the UN Ivan Simonovic says the latest UN Resolution contains a clear message of Croatia's territorial integrity.
- A 412 centimetre shark weighing 330 kilograms is caught in the Omisalj waters near the island of Krk.
- Croatian automobile market: Fiat cars make up 20 percent of newly-purchased vehicles.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA
- Free trade zones in Croatia will help exports and will rake in more money for the economic sector.
- More than 12,000 people attend rock star Sting's concert in Pula. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
